key_insight: pUniFind is a unified deep learning model that can both score peptide-spectrum matches and perform open de novo sequencing, improving proteomics interpretation at large scale. By training on over 100 million spectra, it boosts peptide identification and helps discover previously missed modifications.
problem_solved: Proteomics data analysis is difficult because peptide mass spectra are complex and existing tools often separate peptide identification from de novo sequencing. This paper addresses the need for a single scalable model that can interpret spectra more accurately and uncover modified peptides.
method: Trains a large-scale deep learning model on multimodal data from over 100 million spectra.
Unifies peptide–spectrum scoring and open de novo sequencing into one framework.
Uses the learned representations to improve both peptide identification and modification discovery.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how large-scale multimodal training can unify multiple related inference tasks in a specialized scientific domain. It also demonstrates that foundation-style models can deliver measurable gains in accuracy and discovery for complex biological data.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing spectra input feeding into a unified model with two outputs: scoring and de novo sequencing.
Training scale graphic highlighting "100M+ spectra" and multimodal data sources.
Before-vs-after comparison chart for peptide identification and modification discovery performance.
Spectrum annotation illustration with predicted peptide matches and modification sites.
paper_title: A large-scale unified deep learning model for peptide mass spectrum interpretation trained on multimodal data
paper_authors: Jiale Zhao, Pengzhi Mao, Kaifei Wang, Yiming Li, Yaping Peng
